translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-'ālamīn. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka 'alā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa 'alā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajma'īn. Rabbishraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī, waḥlul 'uqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma 'allimnā mā yanfa'unā, wanfa'nā bimā 'allamtanā, wa zidnā 'ilmā.

text: Last week, we left off at the point where [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] from the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]...

...she came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] looking for a child that she could take with her into the desert and feed that child from her milk, and take care of that child, and let that child grow up in the desert.
And she went to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and she took Muhammad ﷺ.
The mother of Muhammad ﷺ, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], agreed to give her child under the care of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]].

Now, [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] and her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]], they started noticing the [[barakah|بركة]], the blessings, that came into their life after taking this child immediately.

The donkey that they used to come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it was an old and weak and very slow donkey, so slow that [[Halimah|حليمة]] came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] after the rest of the people had already came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
She was late in coming to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] because her transportation, this donkey, was so slow.
So she was late even in coming into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to find a child.

So when she left [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and she had Muhammad ﷺ with her now, this same donkey, now it's the fastest donkey, and it's getting ahead of all of the other donkeys from the other women of the tribe.
Such to the extent that they asked [[Halimah|حليمة]], "[[Halimah|حليمة]], is this the same donkey that you came in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with?
Is it the same donkey? Because at that time it was so slow, and it was lagging behind all of us, and now, it's getting ahead of all of our donkeys. Is it the same donkey?"
And she said, "Yes, it's the same donkey."
And then they said, "This is something amazing. This is something that is astonishing."
Also, as we mentioned last week, [[Halimah|حليمة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she was very poor. Actually, the whole tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were all poor.
And she was from the poorest of them. So poor that she didn't even have enough food for her own self and for her own family.
So she didn't have enough nutrition in her body to produce milk for her own son even. She had her own biological son, who was around the same age as Muhammad ﷺ.
And she didn't even have enough milk for her own son because she wasn't nourished enough. She didn't have enough food to nourish her body to produce that milk.
But once she came back to the desert with Muhammad ﷺ, then she was producing enough milk to fill her own son and Muhammad ﷺ, to fill them, so that they weren't even hungry at all.
These were some of the signs of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into the life of [[Halimah|حليمة]] and her family immediately after bringing the Prophet ﷺ from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] into the desert.
Also, [[Halimah|حليمة]] had a camel, a she-camel, and it was very old.
And its udders had dried up, it wasn't producing any milk anymore because it was so old.
But once she came back with Muhammad ﷺ, then suddenly this old she-camel, it filled up with milk and it started producing milk again.
And the people were surprised, like, "What is happening here?
All of these things are happening, this is something that is not normal."

Another sign of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into their lives after Muhammad ﷺ came with them is that these people of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], the families who lived there, including [[Halimah|حليمة]]'s family, they used to earn money by grazing with livestock.
They had livestock and they used to use that as their source of income. So they had sheep and they had other types of livestock.
And they would have shepherds who would take their sheep out to graze.

But in the middle of the desert, you're not going to find many grazing grounds that can adequately nourish these sheep. You'll find some places here and there, but it really won't be enough to make the sheep very fat.
So all of these sheep from the families of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were all very thin.
And that included [[Halimah|حليمة]]'s sheep as well.

But once Muhammad ﷺ came and was staying with them, then these shepherds, they would take out the sheep of the different families there of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], and [[Halimah|حليمة]]'s sheep, they started getting very fat.
But the sheep of the other families, they still remained very thin, such to the extent that people noticed this, and they started getting mad at the shepherds.
And they would tell the shepherds, "Take our sheep to graze in the same land where [[Halimah|حليمة]]'s sheep are grazing.

You're not doing your job. Her shepherds are taking her sheep to a place where they're getting good food and they're becoming fat, but you guys are taking our sheep, I don't know where you're taking them, you're taking them someplace, but they're not getting fat. Take them to the same place where [[Halimah|حليمة]]'s shepherds are taking her sheep."
And they told the people, "[[Wallahi|والله]], we are taking our sheep to the same place.
We are taking our sheep to the same place, but her sheep are getting fat and ours are not. We don't understand the reasoning behind this."

So these were just some of the glimpses of the [[barakah|بركة]] that came into the life of [[Halimah|حليمة]] and her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]] after they brought this blessed boy, Muhammad ﷺ, to live with them.
And these are the blessings that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave because of the beautiful presence of His greatest creation, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
So he stayed with [[Halimah|حليمة]] for a period of two years.
And this is the milking period. This is the period where the mothers, they feed milk to the children for a period of two years.
So he stayed with her for a period of two years. And in these two years, he grew to be a beautiful young boy, physically strong, and very, very eloquent in his ability to speak as a two-year-old boy.
And there are some kids, MashaAllah, who learn how to speak very early.
And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was one of those boys. At the age of two, he was speaking that pure [[fusha|فصحى]] Arabic eloquently, and clearly, and purely.
So it was very easy for him to speak, and it was very easy for people to understand him from such a young age.
And the tribe of [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they were well-known, they were very well-known as being very, very eloquent in their speech. Their Arabic was the best of the Arabs.
So the Prophet ﷺ, he grew up and he was raised in this type of an environment.
So he grew up, he was physically strong, and he was able to speak eloquently and beautifully at the age of two years old.

And throughout his life, the Prophet ﷺ was known for the eloquence of his speech. There is no speech, after the speech of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], that is more eloquent and more beautiful than the speech of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
And anyone who reads the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, reads the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ, it's very clear. It's very clear that his Arabic, after the Qur'an, it is the best Arabic that you can find.
Such to the extent that [[Abu Bakr|أبو بكر]] [[radiyallahu 'anhu|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ]], he said to the Prophet ﷺ, he said, "[[Ya Rasulullah|يا رسول الله]],"
"I have never heard anyone who has a more eloquent way of speaking than you."
And the Prophet ﷺ replied:

translit: Kayfa lā wa-anā min Quraysh, wa-nasha'tu fī Banī Sa'd?

text: He said, "How can it not be? Of course I am the most eloquent of the Arabs because I am from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and I was brought up with [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]."
So they were known for the eloquence of their language, and the Prophet ﷺ grew up in this type of an environment.

And this is all from the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] did all of this for a reason, so that the Prophet ﷺ had the best possible upbringing.
